# Pinned exceptions to the metaprogramming-word rule of scripts/lean_guard.py `sources` for
# generated files (human decision 2026-11-23, plan step S21). Read by review: this is part of the
# trusted base. Entries:
#   file <path under formal/> sha256 <hex>
#   line <line number> <META word> <exact text of that line>
# A META word in a generated file is excused only at a pinned line number, only if it is the
# pinned word, the line has exactly the pinned text, and the file's bytes have the pinned sha256.
# Any hand edit (which changes the hash) gets the strict rule; stale or unused entries are errors.
# The guard cannot see lexical context: a pinned line is safe only where Lean reads its word
# inside a string literal. So when the translation changes legitimately, regenerate it with
# scripts/aeneas-translate.sh (aeneas-translation.yml must reproduce it byte for byte), read each
# pinned line in context in the new file (no open string or comment before it), and update the
# hash, line numbers and texts here in the same reviewed PR.
#
# T06 `transport.async_rw.is_standard_method` compares the method with the MCP method name
# "initialize", a Lean command keyword.
file translation/Rmcp/Funs.lean sha256 eef79934a10cb94ba4c4d2ce2a5ca98ede7211b8da67a311c593d233137c3900
line 5345 initialize   let b ← Str.Insts.CoreCmpPartialEqStr.eq method (toStr "initialize")
